videos.script: Almost every screen in an app is a list. The planner has three. This lesson is about one question a list keeps asking. Which row is which? {{list}} List draws the rows. ForEach makes a row for each element. Neither is a loop. {{identity}} SwiftUI keeps each row's state by its identity, and in a ForEach the identity is the element's id. {{position}} So you see what happens when the identity is a position instead. You delete one row, and the open notes jump to a row nobody touched. {{swipe}} Sections and swipe actions, and the delete a list hands you. It hands you positions, in the list it showed. {{tests}} The course screen shows one course, and the plan holds them all. So you write the translation from positions to ids, and test it. One test pins the bug. {{lazy}} Then the stacks that build every row at once, and the ones that wait. {{count}} And a count. One session added at the top. One change by id. Five by position.
